questions.stem: A team wants to replace email-based equipment requests with a simple internal app, shared request records, and approval notifications. Which Power Platform approach best fits the scenario?
questions.explanation: Power Apps, Dataverse, and Power Automate map directly to an internal app, shared business data, and approval automation.

options.text: Build a Power Apps app that stores requests in Dataverse and starts a Power Automate approval
options.explanation: This combines the app, governed data, and workflow services described in the scenario.

options.text: Keep a personal Excel file and email each request manually
options.explanation: A personal file and email thread do not provide shared governed records or automated approvals.

options.text: Use only Power Pages for an anonymous public website
options.explanation: The requirement is an internal app and approval process, not an external website.

questions.stem: Which **two** practices support business value when makers use AI-assisted Power Platform creation?
questions.explanation: AI assistance accelerates drafting, but business value still depends on human validation and least-privilege governance.

options.text: Review generated apps, tables, flows, or topics before publishing them
options.explanation: AI output is a draft and should be checked for business fit, security, and accessibility.

options.text: Assign users only the permissions they need for the solution
options.explanation: Least privilege protects data while still allowing users to complete their work.

options.text: Skip governance because low-code assets are automatically safe
options.explanation: Low-code solutions still require environments, roles, policies, and lifecycle controls.

options.text: Use one shared admin account for every maker and tester
options.explanation: Shared elevated accounts remove accountability and violate least-privilege governance.

questions.stem: Order the dependent steps for releasing a model-driven app to users.
questions.explanation: The data model defines the app structure, the completed app is published, and only then can users be shared into that published app experience with the right role.

items.text: Model the Dataverse tables, columns, and relationships
Build or generate the model-driven app from that model
Share the published app with users by assigning the appropriate security role

explanations.s1: The Dataverse model must exist before the model-driven app can use its tables, forms, and relationships.
explanations.s2: The app can be built only after the underlying model is available.
explanations.s3: Users need a published app version before there is a released experience to share.
explanations.s4: Sharing with the right security role comes last so users receive access to the published app and governed data.

questions.stem: A maker is building a canvas app and needs a Save button to write the current edit form back to Dataverse. Which formula should the button use?
questions.explanation: SubmitForm submits the current values from an edit form to its data source, which matches the Save button requirement.

options.text: `SubmitForm(EditForm1)`
options.explanation: This submits the form values to the connected data source.

options.text: `ResetForm(EditForm1)`
options.explanation: ResetForm discards edits and returns the form to its initial state; it does not save the row.

options.text: `Navigate(EditForm1)`
options.explanation: Navigate changes screens and does not submit an edit form.
